summary: Today's decisions still look sound after the close, and one day's P&L doesn't change that. Both trades filled at the open. MSM was sold in full at $121.45 against the $118.72 cost, a short-term gain of about $0.18. INCY was bought at $119.37 for about $15.0 and closed at $122.27 (+2.4%). Equity is $626.06 (+$3.53, +0.57%). SPY gained about 1.3% on the same day, so the Market Analyst's low-conviction risk-on call was right for one session and the book lagged it. That lag is the expected cost of a defensive, low-beta book holding about 10% cash: invested is 89.7% against the shadow's 99.5%, and the 10%-drop stress is about -$22.7, roughly 3.6% of equity. Over the whole run the stock picks are not the problem. Invested return is +5.04% for the agent against +4.42% for the shadow, while total return is +4.34% against +4.42%, so the remaining gap is cash drag. The rotation followed the stated tilt (Health Care favored, Industrials avoided). It was sized for the IDXX overlap, with Health Care now about 10.5% by bucket, and it kept the cash buffer. The Skeptic's FAST-versus-MSM point was answered honestly as a risk call, not a quality call. The stop-storage work landed: every position now has a numeric stop and none shows 'missing'. No price stop or qualitative clause tripped today. The two stop_alerts (BND and IEF, both NEAR at +1.6%) come from how tight I set those stops, not from today's move: BND fell 0.14% and IEF 0.07%. I am not tagging them broken. Weak points: (1) INCY's stored invalidation still measures the $110 stop from the 11-10 reference close and says it 'will be restated'. That is the conditional text L6 warns against, and against the actual fill $110 is about 7.9% lower, not 10%. (2) INCY's 'trails XLV by more than 8 points over 21 days' clause cannot be checked unless INCY's own price series is in the packet, which the Skeptic flagged and I accepted without a fix. (3) The BND thesis I stored carries a weight figure ('near 9% of equity'), which L6 says to keep out. (4) WMT's $116 stop is a close-based stop. It does not protect against a gap through it on the approximate 11-19 print, so the tighter stop is weaker protection than I implied while the Skeptic's trim case stands unanswered.
lessons: At the next run, use thesis_updates to restate INCY's invalidation against the $119.37 fill ($110 is about 7.9% under it) and drop the 'will be restated' wording. Also remove the weight figure from BND's stored thesis (L6).

Don't store an invalidation clause that today's inputs can't measure. If a relative-performance clause needs a held name's own price series (INCY against XLV), confirm the series is in the packet. If it isn't, replace the clause with a measurable one through thesis_updates (L7).

BND and IEF stops sit about 1.6% under the mark and roughly 1.8-1.9% under the fills, which an ordinary few-week rates move can reach. When either shows NEAR, decide ahead of time whether the bond sleeve is ballast (widen the stop or rest it on the 200-day test) or a rate-shock exit (let it trip), so a trip doesn't sell both at once by accident.

A close-based stop is not pre-earnings protection. For a near-cap holding going into a print with an unconfirmed date (WMT about 11.9%, approximately 11-19, entering the window 11-12), ask the Proposer for a trim proposal rather than relying on a tighter stop. If none comes, say plainly in the reasoning that the gap risk is accepted.

Under a risk-on stance, the book's low beta and roughly 10% cash will lag rally days like today. That is acceptable while invested returns beat the shadow's, but keep deploying cash above the 10% buffer into stated tilts when sized proposals come, and don't let low conviction turn into idle cash.
